submissions.title: Memphis City Council declines to pass data center moratorium
submissions.excerpt: The 12-month moratorium vote tied 6-6; council instead passed a 135-day pause on data center permitting.

submissions.title: Aurora City Council votes down indefinite data center moratorium
submissions.excerpt: Six councilmembers voted for the indefinite moratorium and five against; a two-thirds majority was required to pass.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Aurora, CO city council rejected an indefinite data center moratorium on 2026-10-26 (6-5, short of the required two-thirds). This is the second such rejection; an earlier 6-month moratorium was rejected in August. In the same session the council advanced a new zoning rule requiring data centers to sit at least 750 feet from residentially zoned districts. Separately (reported same week), Vantage, developer of the nearby Trident Data Center, agreed to seek an alternative site; the moratorium would not have applied to Trident regardless since it would not affect already-submitted applications. submissions.title: Davidson County adopts stricter data center rules, rejects moratorium
submissions.excerpt: Commissioners voted 5-2 to adopt new data center restrictions in place of a proposed four-month moratorium.
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Davidson County, NC board of commissioners rejected a proposed 4-month data center moratorium on 2026-10-26 and instead voted 5-2 to adopt new rules covering noise, water and power use, and environmental impact for future data center proposals in unincorporated county areas. Officials say no data center applications have been submitted in the county so far, so no specific project is attached to this finding.
